item.title: 🎧 LISTEN #1 — Jason & Scot Show: EP344 - How Brooklinen Is Preparing for Agentic Commerce
item.ns1:encoded:
Score: 88/100 | Listen Fully | Confidence: low

Originally published 07 Aug 2026

This episode directly addresses key focus areas: eCommerce, AI/emerging technology (agentic commerce), and product strategy. It provides concrete insights from an industry operator on how a digital-first brand is adapting to future retail trends, making it highly actionable and strategically important.

Summary

Live from NRF Nexus, Jason and Scot interview Abbie Weiss, SVP of Digital & E-Commerce at Brooklinen, about the brand's strategy for digital-first retail and its preparation for 'agentic commerce.' The discussion covers Brooklinen's expansion into retail, B2B, and design trade, emphasizing customer experience and ease. They explore the changing landscape of product discovery, the role of influencers, and the blurring lines between awareness and conversion. Abbie details how Brooklinen is future-proofing its operations through enhanced content, catalog readiness, and cross-team collaboration to leverage emerging AI-driven commerce agents.

Key Ideas

  • Strategies for preparing for 'agentic commerce' and AI's impact on retail.
  • Evolving customer discovery and conversion in digital-first retail.
  • Cross-channel expansion and customer experience as core strategy.

Implications

Provides highly relevant and actionable insights for product leaders in eCommerce and retail. It offers a practical case study on how a digital-first brand is adapting its product and marketing strategies to emerging AI technologies and changing consumer behaviors, directly informing strategic decisions for future-proofing and growth.

item.title: 🎧 LISTEN #2 — Acquired: Disney: The Renaissance and the Empire
item.ns1:encoded:
Score: 84/100 | Listen Fully | Confidence: low

Originally published 10 Aug 2026

This episode offers a deep, strategic dive into corporate turnarounds, M&A, and long-term product/brand portfolio management at an empire scale. The lessons on strategic pivots, market dynamics, and leadership are highly relevant for a Senior PM focused on product strategy and career growth, despite not being directly about AI or eCommerce.

Summary

This extensive episode from Acquired chronicles the tumultuous history of the Walt Disney Company, from near bankruptcy in 1984 to its resurgence under Michael Eisner and Frank Wells, marked by iconic animation, Broadway expansion, and the acquisition of ESPN. It then details the subsequent challenges, including executive infighting and a hostile takeover attempt by Comcast, leading to another epic comeback under Bob Iger with strategic acquisitions like Pixar, Marvel, and Lucasfilm. The narrative provides a masterclass in corporate strategy, M&A, brand management, and navigating market shifts to build and sustain a global media empire.

Key Ideas

  • Corporate turnaround strategies and leadership in crisis.
  • Strategic M&A for portfolio growth and market dominance.
  • Long-term brand management and product flywheel development.

Implications

Provides a rich case study for understanding long-term product strategy, portfolio management, and the role of M&A in building and defending market leadership. Offers transferable lessons on strategic foresight, navigating complex market dynamics, and the importance of leadership in driving innovation and growth at scale.
